pr_title: Auto recover when the Bluetooth adapter stops responding
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->


Some adapters stop responding after running the scanner for a few hours.  

This has mostly been reported with the Realtek chipsets, however since they seem to have the largest market share, it is not know if they are the only chip affected since number of reports vs actual distribution of deployed devices is impossible to ever know. Its also been reported that disabling USB auto power management may improve the reliability here https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/76544#issuecomment-1221272935

If scanner stops responding and the restart does not fix it, the next attempt will cycle the device to get it working again.

This also allows recovery when the docker container is restarted at inopportune time (i.e. in the middle of the scanner startup process)

This should resolve at least 6 of the issues in the bluetooth issues in the queue (probably more)

~~TODO~~:
- [x] Tests
- [x] Actually call the library to recover the adapter (make https://github.com/custom-components/ble_monitor/blob/master/custom_components/ble_monitor/bt_helpers.py into a library since its already been solved there), Needs to be asyncio friendly though (remove sleeps, run in executor, etc)
- [x] Link issues
- [x] Don't wait to do the reset if we are stuck in an InProgress state
- [x] Adjust startup timeout to 15s, and do the reset if we timeout because its the same issue
- [x] Handle timeout case
- [x] Handle `org.bluez.Error.InProgress` case
- [x] Handle `org.bluez.Error.NotReady` case

issue_context.title: Xiaomi (LYWSDCGQ) stops reporting state with new Bluetooth integration
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hi,

I was using BLE Monitor (https://github.com/custom-components/ble_monitor) and after finding out they will phase out their integration for the new HA Bluetooth integration I thought I'd make the switch.

I deleted the BLE Monitor install which worked perfectly and setup the Bluetooth HA version. Everything worked for a few minutes and I didn't bother to check the state of my devices again. I went on holiday for 3 days and when I came back home the state had not changed for 3 days and only one of my 2 devices were showing as unavailable. I then restarted my server and both devices were showing as Unavailable. After a few resets I can get it working for a few minutes again but then it stops.

I am running the Bluetooth of my ASUS NUC. This never had a problem with BLE Monitor so I don't think that would be the issue. I even tried a Bluetooth dongle and that also works only for a few minutes then stops reporting the current state.

also opened a issue with BLE Monitor: https://github.com/custom-components/ble_monitor/issues/984

I don't have any other Bluetooth integrations installed

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.8.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

BLE Monitor

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Bluetooth

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/bluetooth/

### Diagnostics information

No "Download diagnostic" option for Bluetooth or the Devices.

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Logger: homeassistant.components.bluetooth
Source: components/bluetooth/__init__.py:422
Integration: Bluetooth (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 9:40:48 AM (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 9:40:48 AM

Error stopping scanner: [org.bluez.Error.InProgress] Operation already in progress
```


### Additional information
Virtual VM shows this:
